title: Using weak hashing algorithms is security-sensitive
description: Cryptographic hash functions are essential for data integrity verification and digital signatures. However, weak hashing algorithms like MD2, MD4, MD5, SHA-1, and RIPEMD are vulnerable to collision attacks where different inputs produce the same hash output. This vulnerability can be exploited by attackers to forge digital signatures, compromise data integrity checks, or perform other cryptographic attacks. Modern applications should use stronger alternatives like SHA-256, SHA-3, or BLAKE2 that are resistant to known cryptographic attacks.
message: Make sure this weak hash algorithm is not used in a security context here.

impact.security: High impact as weak hashing algorithms can be exploited for collision attacks, allowing attackers to forge digital signatures or compromise data integrity
impact.reliability: Medium impact on system reliability due to potential security breaches and compromised data validation

recommendation: Replace weak hashing algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, etc.) with stronger alternatives like SHA-256, SHA-3, or BLAKE2. For password hashing, use specialized algorithms like bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.

references.title: SonarSource Python Rules - Using weak hashing algorithms is security-sensitive

noncompliant.code:
import hashlib

# Noncompliant: MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks
hash_md5 = hashlib.md5()
hash_md5.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_md5.hexdigest()

import hashlib

# Noncompliant: SHA-1 is vulnerable to collision attacks
hash_sha1 = hashlib.sha1()
hash_sha1.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_sha1.hexdigest()

import hashlib

# Noncompliant: MD2 is cryptographically broken
hash_md2 = hashlib.new('md2')
hash_md2.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_md2.hexdigest()

noncompliant.description: Using weak hash in security context

noncompliant.code:
import hashlib

# Noncompliant: Direct instantiation of weak algorithms
md5_hash = hashlib.md5(b"data")
sha1_hash = hashlib.sha1(b"data")
md4_hash = hashlib.new('md4', b"data")

compliant.code:
import hashlib

# Compliant: SHA-256 is cryptographically secure
hash_sha256 = hashlib.sha256()
hash_sha256.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_sha256.hexdigest()

import hashlib

# Compliant: SHA-3 provides strong security
hash_sha3 = hashlib.sha3_256()
hash_sha3.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_sha3.hexdigest()

import hashlib

# Compliant: BLAKE2 is a secure modern hash function
hash_blake2 = hashlib.blake2b()
hash_blake2.update(b"Hello World")
digest = hash_blake2.hexdigest()

import bcrypt

# Compliant: bcrypt is designed for password hashing
password = b"my_password"
hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(password, bcrypt.gensalt())

compliant.description: Using secure hash in security context

devsecops.remediation_guidance: Replace with SHA-256 or stronger algorithms

why_is_this_an_issue: Weak hashing algorithms like MD5 and SHA-1 are vulnerable to collision attacks where attackers can find different inputs that produce the same hash output. This vulnerability undermines the security guarantees that hash functions are supposed to provide, such as data integrity verification and digital signature security. In security-sensitive contexts, these weaknesses can be exploited to forge documents, bypass authentication mechanisms, or compromise cryptographic protocols. Modern cryptographic standards recommend against using these algorithms in favor of stronger alternatives that are resistant to known attacks.

how_to_fix.description: Identify all uses of weak hashing algorithms (MD2, MD4, MD5, SHA-1, RIPEMD) in your code
For general-purpose hashing, replace with SHA-256, SHA-3, or BLAKE2
For password hashing, use specialized algorithms like bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2
Update any stored hash values to use the new algorithm format
Ensure compatibility with existing systems that may rely on the hash format
Test thoroughly to ensure the new hashing implementation works correctly
Update documentation to reflect the new hashing algorithm choice

conditions.comment: Detect direct calls to weak hash algorithms like hashlib.md5(), hashlib.sha1(), etc.
Detect hashlib.new() with weak algorithms passed as string argument
